representationConvention.nonAbelian: Highest-weight Dynkin labels, one nonnegative integer per node
representationConvention.nodeNumbering: Bourbaki numbering, as in Sage finite Cartan types
representationConvention.abelian: Exact charges in the recorded factor basis and common normalization
representationConvention.unresolved: ?; a source dimension is never substituted for a missing Dynkin label
representationConvention.dimensionShorthandD: For odd D_r, the penultimate spinor node is unbarred and its dual is barred in dimension shorthand; exact Dynkin labels remain the identifiers

fourDimensions.fermionBasis: Independent left-handed Weyl fields only. A RH field is replaced by its LH charge conjugate: conjugate every non-Abelian irrep and negate every U(1) charge. A Dirac field is two LH fields in R and conjugate(R).

lorentzConvention.higherDimensions: Complexified B/D Dynkin labels; standard vector node first and spinor node(s) last. No dimensional reduction is inferred.
lorentzConvention.scope: Finite-dimensional Lorentz field representations, not on-shell polarization counts or Poincare particle representations.
lorentzConvention.unrecordedDimension: Ordinary non-bulk field descriptions use an explicitly marked editorial 4D interpretation. Bulk/extra-dimensional descriptions with missing dimension remain unresolved. Brane fields are distinguished from bulk fields.

scalarConvention.unit: One irreducible real gauge module per scalar copy
scalarConvention.realType: Real form of the displayed complex highest-weight irrep; an unconstrained complex field contributes two copies
scalarConvention.complexType: Underlying real module of R; R and its full conjugate specify the same real module
scalarConvention.pseudorealType: Underlying real module; no half-dimensional ordinary real form is imposed
scalarConvention.orientation: First nonzero Abelian charge positive; otherwise lexicographically larger weight tuple, in factor order
scalarConvention.missing: Unestablished scalar counting is pending extraction, not a completed canonical row
scalarConvention.method: Tits theorem 3.6; exact finite Cartan matrices and dominant dual weights

coreConvention.projection: Restrict the full matter representation to the semisimple gauge algebra; omit every Abelian factor, including hypercharge
coreConvention.counting: Preserve Lorentz representations and real scalar degrees of freedom; decompose and aggregate copy counts after restriction
coreConvention.identity: Gauge-factor/row order and identical-factor permutations removed; no general simple-algebra outer-automorphism quotient
coreConvention.meaning: Coarse grouping, not physical-theory equivalence, symmetry breaking, or an SM-embedding certificate

semisimpleConvention.projection: Retain the multiset of resolved canonical simple gauge factors independently of matter-inventory completeness; omit every Abelian factor
semisimpleConvention.meaning: Derived algebra-only grouping, not a global group, quotient, physical theory or additional source inventory

fullAlgebraConvention.projection: Retain canonical simple factors and the number of u(1) factors; omit matter, charges and source generator names
fullAlgebraConvention.meaning: Abstract local gauge algebra, not a choice of Abelian basis, global group or quotient

claims.locator: Section 2, PDF/printed pp.4-6 Eqs.(3),(5),(8), heavy-Higgs paragraph and Eq.(15)
claims.value: Phi is an unconstrained complex bidoublet: source has two SU(2)_L doublets and a complex heavy neutral component, not a single real bidoublet. Delta_L/R are complex since their continuous B-L charge is nonzero. No dependent conjugate multiplets are counted.

claims.locator: Section 2, PDF/printed p.5 generation-indices sentence after Eq.(8); p.6 Eq.(11); section 4.1, PDF/printed p.22 Flavor structure
claims.value: Eq.(11) enumerates u,c,t and d,s,b in both chiralities, fixing three quark families. p.22 explicitly describes the three nu_R mass eigenstates; combined with Eq.(1), the lepton doublets have three copies.

claims.locator: Section 2, PDF/printed p.4 explicitly suppresses colour; p.4 Eq.(1); p.4 Eqs.(3)-(4)
claims.value: Restore the ordinary SM colour algebra su(3), fundamental quarks and singlet leptons/Higgs. This is expansion of the paper's explicitly suppressed ordinary colour sector using the atlas SM baseline, not a new colour tuple printed by P04. No global quotient is asserted.

claims.locator: Section 2, PDF/printed p.4 Eqs.(1)-(2)
claims.value: Using the ordinary identified u,d charges 2/3,-1/3 and nu,e charges 0,-1, Eq.(2) gives source B-L=1/3 for Q_L/R and -1 for l_L/R. The opposite SU(2) factor acts trivially. These charges are derived, not a fermion charge table quoted from P04.

claims.locator: lr-source-candidate.json and lr-preflight.json
claims.value: One positive primitive scale 3 over fermions AND scalars: q=3(B-L). Source Q_R,l_R convert to LH conjugates with colour conjugation and charges -1,+3; triplets have +6. The source coupling on p.5 multiplies (B-L)/2, so g_atlas=g_source/6 if that covariant-derivative convention is retained.

claims.locator: Section 2, PDF/printed p.7 Eqs.(16)-(17)
claims.value: P exchanges Q_L and Q_R and maps Phi to Phi^dagger; C exchanges Q_L with (Q_R)^c and maps Phi to Phi^T. Hermitian versus symmetric Yukawa restrictions differ. Both use the same gauge/matter inventory, hence ONE staged field-content candidate with two source variants.

reextractions.limitations: Scoped gauge/matter review, not an independent physics, anomaly, viability or whole-paper verification. Legacy assertions remain unchanged. Scalar-realification equivalence is not yet canonicalized.

fields.label: Ŝ
fields.sourceNote: Gauge singlet. Unhatted S is its complex scalar component; ψS is its fermionic component. These are not additional independent supermultiplets.

evidence.claim: The general NMSSM is defined as the MSSM with one additional gauge-singlet chiral superfield Ŝ and the most general renormalisable superpotential couplings and corresponding soft terms within the stated symmetry assumptions.

Hatted capital letters denote chiral superfields; unhatted capital letters denote their complex scalar components. Thus S is the complex scalar component of Ŝ, not an additional independent multiplet.
The baseline construction retains the SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1)Y gauge sector; the added S carries no quantum numbers under these factors.

spacetime.note: Supersymmetric light gauge-basis EFT below heavy messenger masses; one or two singlet chiral multiplets, before horizontal-field removal.

fields.conversion: Full source inventory, primitive integer charges, LH fermions and real-module scalar counting.

evidence.claim: The source treats supersymmetric SM extensions. Three ordinary quark generations carry explicitly stated GSM representations. The low-energy regime has two Higgs doublets, singlet scalars S1,S2 (or explicitly replaced by one S), and three light charged-lepton generations after heavy-field removal. Horizontal continuous charges are bookkeeping for a discrete symmetry, not additional local U1 gauge factors.

In this source SUSY regime, the displayed charged scalar/matter fields belong to chiral multiplets (one complex scalar plus one LH Weyl); GSM vector multiplets supply one adjoint gaugino per factor. The declared MSSM template expands this implication. No auxiliary fields or dependent conjugates count as matter.

Preserve apparent source typographical conflicts instead of silently certifying them.

Eq42 contains(S_A^dagger sigma^a S_A)T_j^a and(H^dagger sigma^a H)T_j^a,epsilon_abc T_i^a T_j^b T_k^c; a is weak-adjoint index and j=1..3 labels triplets. Source explicitly says SU2 indices on H and S are suppressed. Thus S is the original weak DOUBLEt, and T consists of THREE real weak TRIPLET copies, colour-singletY0. The SectionVIII(8,1) label and conclusion(1,2) label conflict with these explicit tensors, not with each other as viable alternatives: Pauli-matrix bilinears and epsilon_abc fix the displayed construction. Preserve these source misprints in evidence instead of treating a bare dimension as authoritative or pretending they never occurred.

fields.conversion: Full source inventory, primitive integer charges, LH fermions and real-module scalar counting.

evidence.claim: The source specifies GSM×U1F, three SM chiral families plus three singlet RH neutrinos and one Higgs H with source Y=-1/2. All SM Yukawa couplings force universal Q,uR,dR,L,eR charges and fix FH via Eq5.2; RH-neutrino charges may remain family-dependent. No requirement to specify a neutrino mass mechanism is imposed on the gauge-matter inventory.

Define q=FQ, r=(Fn1+Fn2+Fn3)/3. Eq3.1 with universal SM species gives Fu=4q+r,Fd=-2q-r,FL=-3q,Fe=-6q-r;Eq5.2 gives FH=-3q-r. With ni=Fνi, the source conditions are sum ni=3r and sum ni^3=3r^3; these are source-family relations, not a new atlas anomaly gate. RHS ν_i become LH conjugates with X=-ni. The universal QYBL subfamily sets all ni=r; r!=0 retains the nonzero B-L component of P13 Eq45. Positive-Y atlas Higgs is the full scalar conjugate; no extra Higgs is added.

The rendered Eq3.2 prints Fe=FQ-Fu, inconsistent with Eq3.1 and the charged-lepton Yukawa relation. Use the unambiguous Eq3.1 sum relation Fe=-6q-r and retain this visible source discrepancy; do not silently trust the text extraction.

fields.label: Q scalar

spacetime.note: Fresh full rendered pages9-11;SectionIII.A.3 andTableII, with same-section context

fields.conversion: Full source inventory, primitive integer charges, LH fermions and real-module scalar counting.

evidence.claim: The paper explicitly considers an E6-inspired GSM×U1 construction, not a full E6 GUT. It specifies the supersymmetric model with three complete27 chiral multiplets and allows a Hu,Hd pair inside these27s to serve as MSSM Higgs. This accepted target narrows the earlier uninstantiated charge template to the source-explicit psi benchmark theta=pi/2.

Use primitive qpsi=2sqrt(6)Qpsi. Each16 has qpsi=1; each10 has qpsi=-2; singletS has qpsi=4. The16 decomposes to Q,u^c,e^c,d^c,L,nu^c; the10 to D,D^c,Hu,Hd. Source D is colour3,Y=-1/3 and Dc its conjugate; Hu,Hd are weak doublets,Y=+/-1/2. Every such chiral multiplet occurs3times. Exact A2 weights distinguish3 andbar3; A1doublet=[1].

Each source chiral multiplet contributes one source complex scalar and one LH Weyl. Include the four gauge-factor gauginos as adjoint LH Weyl fields, not gauge connections. Hypercharge qY=6Y and qpsi=2sqrt(6)Qpsi are each primitive across full spectrum. Scalar real-module orientation conjugates all factors simultaneously when required.

The additionalHu+Huc pair from an incomplete27+27bar is an optional repair of simple unification. It is not in the explicitly preceding three-complete27 model. Failure of simple gauge unification is not an atlas exclusion criterion. OtherE6benchmarks/nonSUSYcompletions are not united with this inventory.

claims.fact: The paper explicitly considers an E6-inspired GSM×U1 construction, not a full E6 GUT. It specifies the supersymmetric model with three complete27 chiral multiplets and allows a Hu,Hd pair inside these27s to serve as MSSM Higgs. This accepted target narrows the earlier uninstantiated charge template to the source-explicit psi benchmark theta=pi/2.

Use primitive qpsi=2sqrt(6)Qpsi. Each16 has qpsi=1; each10 has qpsi=-2; singletS has qpsi=4. The16 decomposes to Q,u^c,e^c,d^c,L,nu^c; the10 to D,D^c,Hu,Hd. Source D is colour3,Y=-1/3 and Dc its conjugate; Hu,Hd are weak doublets,Y=+/-1/2. Every such chiral multiplet occurs3times. Exact A2 weights distinguish3 andbar3; A1doublet=[1].

Each source chiral multiplet contributes one source complex scalar and one LH Weyl. Include the four gauge-factor gauginos as adjoint LH Weyl fields, not gauge connections. Hypercharge qY=6Y and qpsi=2sqrt(6)Qpsi are each primitive across full spectrum. Scalar real-module orientation conjugates all factors simultaneously when required.

The additionalHu+Huc pair from an incomplete27+27bar is an optional repair of simple unification. It is not in the explicitly preceding three-complete27 model. Failure of simple gauge unification is not an atlas exclusion criterion. OtherE6benchmarks/nonSUSYcompletions are not united with this inventory.

limitations: Scope deliberately selects the explicitly named source psi benchmark and supersymmetric three27 branch; it does not claim to resolve the entire continuous E6 angle family.
No full gaugedE6 GUT or GUT-breaking spectrum is inferred.
Kinetic mixing changes gauge coupling/current basis, not the specified Y,psi generator representations; no source effective-charge epsilonY is misstored as a new matter charge.
Optional extra incomplete27 Higgs pair not appended, and no unification/viability gate imposed.

fields.label: Q1

spacetime.note: Minimal electroweak-symmetric GSM×U1F EFT specified by Eq4.2, including its explicit single Higgs.

fields.conversion: Full source inventory, primitive integer charges, LH fermions and real-module scalar counting.

evidence.claim: Full GSM×U1F algebra and three copies of Q,L,eR,uR,dR; the selected SM (not SMνR) assignment has no added singlet neutrinos. Higgs is source (1,2,-1/2).

Weak-basis families are Q=(0,-3,3),eR=(0,-3,3),uR=(0,-1,1),L=(0,-4,4),dR=(0,0,0), and one source Higgs has FH=+2. This is a defined minimal gauge-basis EFT; the later broken-Zprime and UV-Yukawa applications are conditional and not an asserted extra field inventory.

Set qY=6Y jointly, with all charges primitive across every fermion and scalar; conjugate RH fields on all gauge factors. Expand generation charge lists into individual rows. Source H has qY=-3,F=2; its canonical real-module representative is the full conjugate, qY=3,F=-2.

notes: No massive broken-Zprime completion or UV messenger spectrum is claimed. Source applications after symmetry breaking require additional model building; the accepted object is the explicitly specified gauge-basis EFT.

fields.label: Q

spacetime.note: Minimal gauge-basis GSM×U1F spectrum with three singlet neutrinos, one Higgs and source-defined polynomial charge parameters.

fields.conversion: Full source inventory, primitive integer charges, LH fermions and real-module scalar counting.

evidence.claim: The source specifies GSM×U1F, three SM chiral families plus three singlet RH neutrinos and one Higgs H with source Y=-1/2. All SM Yukawa couplings force universal Q,uR,dR,L,eR charges and fix FH via Eq5.2; RH-neutrino charges may remain family-dependent. No requirement to specify a neutrino mass mechanism is imposed on the gauge-matter inventory.

Define q=FQ, r=(Fn1+Fn2+Fn3)/3. Eq3.1 with universal SM species gives Fu=4q+r,Fd=-2q-r,FL=-3q,Fe=-6q-r;Eq5.2 gives FH=-3q-r. With ni=Fνi, the source conditions are sum ni=3r and sum ni^3=3r^3; these are source-family relations, not a new atlas anomaly gate. RHS ν_i become LH conjugates with X=-ni. The universal QYBL subfamily sets all ni=r; r!=0 retains the nonzero B-L component of P13 Eq45. Positive-Y atlas Higgs is the full scalar conjugate; no extra Higgs is added.

The rendered Eq3.2 prints Fe=FQ-Fu, inconsistent with Eq3.1 and the charged-lepton Yukawa relation. Use the unambiguous Eq3.1 sum relation Fe=-6q-r and retain this visible source discrepancy; do not silently trust the text extraction.

fields.label: lepton triplets

spacetime.note: SectionII Eqs.(3)-(10), PDFpp3-5; SectionIII after Eq.(40), PDFp12

fields.conversion: Full source inventory, primitive integer charges, LH fermions and real-module scalar counting.

evidence.claim: One first-family quark SU(3)L triplet with N=2/3, two anti-triplets with N=-1/3, three lepton triplets N=0 containing charged antileptons; no RH neutrinos. RH quarks are SU(3)L singlets, usual u/d N=2/3,-1/3, exotic J1=5/3 and two J=-4/3. Explicit colour counted for anomalies. Scalars eta,rho,chi are complex SU(3)L triplets of N=0,+1,-1. Normalize whole spectrum by q=3N; conjugate every RH colour and charge.

evidence.claim: MSSM N=1 matter and both Hu,Hd retained; add one adjoint chiral Aj for each Gi=SU3,SU2,U1. Each Aj contains complex scalar and independent LH Weyl, with exact weights SU3 adjoint[1,1],SU2 adjoint[2],U1 adjoint singlet. Therefore complex neutral real-type Aj scalar gives two real-module copies; fermion gives one Weyl. MSSM adjoint gaugino already counted, so Dirac gauginos are not additional fermions on top of both Weyl constituents.

evidence.claim: Source explicitly defines renormalizable effective theory with soft breaking and external W'alpha/M=theta_alpha mD spurion. No bulk/brane or unified regime is summed into this 4D EFT.

evidence.claim: The source treats supersymmetric SM extensions. Three ordinary quark generations carry explicitly stated GSM representations. The low-energy regime has two Higgs doublets, singlet scalars S1,S2 (or explicitly replaced by one S), and three light charged-lepton generations after heavy-field removal. Horizontal continuous charges are bookkeeping for a discrete symmetry, not additional local U1 gauge factors.

In this source SUSY regime, the displayed charged scalar/matter fields belong to chiral multiplets (one complex scalar plus one LH Weyl); GSM vector multiplets supply one adjoint gaugino per factor. The declared MSSM template expands this implication. No auxiliary fields or dependent conjugates count as matter.

evidence.claim: One complex H=(A,B) with A the ordinary SM Higgs and B one twin weak doublet. The paper explicitly keeps the radial mode rather than choosing its nonlinear alternative. B is SM neutral; its neutral twin weak doublet is pseudoreal, so one source complex B is one underlying real module.
Twin su(2) and su(3) are gauged. Twin hypercharge is explicitly not included in the minimal model. The complete algebra is g_SM plus twin su(3) plus twin su(2), not a dark-sector-only algebra.

RH fields convert to LH conjugates across all factors.

spacetime.note: Source-explicit delta=1 specialization, five-dimensional SM bulk action on S1/Z2, existing regime147. No summation with generic-dimension, six-dimensional or KK description regimes.

fields.conversion: Full source inventory with dimension-appropriate Lorentz representations; physical source gauge representations retained without a 4D chirality conversion.

evidence.claim: Bulk g_SM, three families of Q,U,D,L,E and one scalar doublet H. Eq.(2.1) suppresses leptons for brevity but explicitly includes them on the next page. Yukawa matrices are3x3. Physical gauge reps are Q=(3,2,1/6),U=(3,1,2/3),D=(3,1,-1/3),L=(1,2,-1/2),E=(1,1,-1),H=(1,2,1/2).

locations.locator: PDF p.3 Section2 Eq.(2.1) and following paragraphs; p.4 opening sentence

evidence.claim: Source explicitly specializes delta=1, using S1/Z2. Odd-dimensional Q,U,D,L,E are vector-like four-component spinors, not 4D Weyl fields. Lorentz complexified so5=B2 spinor labels are[0,1]; scalar labels[0,0]. No RH-to-LH gauge conjugation or Dirac splitting is applied to a 5D spinor.

locations.locator: PDF p.4 odd-dimension spinor paragraph and orbifold prescription; p.5 paragraph immediately after Eq.(2.3)

evidence.claim: Save the finite bulk inventory. Gauge potentials A_alpha are implied connections; their lower-dimensional components and infinite KK modes are not independent matter appended to this five-dimensional description. No unspecified higher-dimensional anomaly-cancelling fields are imported from the even-dimension discussion.
The complete five-dimensional inventory has source hypercharges with common primitive normalization q=6Y: Q1,U4,D-2,L-3,E-6,H3. Keeping U,D,E in physical gauge reps is essential in 5D.

fields.label: Q

spacetime.note: Microscopic Simple v-Model of Table I, specialized only to the paper's explicit n_v=3, k=0, q_+=-2 benchmark below Eq. (3); before hidden confinement and U(1) breaking.

fields.conversion: Full source inventory, primitive integer charges, LH fermions and real-module scalar counting.

evidence.claim: Full SM plus su(n_v) and u(1)_chi. Two hidden flavours U,Ubar and C,Cbar are fundamental/antifundamental; exactly three neutrino singlets N_i and one charged complex phi. All SM fields are valley neutral. Table uses common LH chiral coordinates q,ubar,dbar,L,eplus; N=-1 is interpreted in that same chiral coordinate, with source prose right-handed-species naming retained.

locations.locator: PDF p.1 Simple v-Model and Table I

evidence.claim: The paper explicitly uses n_v=3, kinetic mixing k=0, q_+=-2. The Table I relation q_++q_-=-2 gives q_-=0. Thus U,Ubar,C,Cbar charges are -2,0,+2,0. This numerical benchmark is not a replacement for the entire free-rank/free-charge family.

Multiply source hypercharge by6 and chi charge by5 jointly over the complete spectrum. Standard family chi charges become (-1,-1,3,3,-1); N=-5, H=2, phi=10, hidden flavour charges (-10,0,10,0). Three ordinary SM families are inherited; the source independently fixes exactly three N_i.

inspection.scope: Microscopic Simple v-Model of Table I, specialized only to the paper's explicit n_v=3, k=0, q_+=-2 benchmark below Eq. (3); before hidden confinement and U(1) breaking.

claims.locator: PDF p.1 Simple v-Model and Table I
claims.fact: Full SM plus su(n_v) and u(1)_chi. Two hidden flavours U,Ubar and C,Cbar are fundamental/antifundamental; exactly three neutrino singlets N_i and one charged complex phi. All SM fields are valley neutral. Table uses common LH chiral coordinates q,ubar,dbar,L,eplus; N=-1 is interpreted in that same chiral coordinate, with source prose right-handed-species naming retained.

claims.locator: PDF p.2 below Eq. (3)
claims.fact: The paper explicitly uses n_v=3, kinetic mixing k=0, q_+=-2. The Table I relation q_++q_-=-2 gives q_-=0. Thus U,Ubar,C,Cbar charges are -2,0,+2,0. This numerical benchmark is not a replacement for the entire free-rank/free-charge family.

claims.locator: PDF p.1 Table I; Atlas full-inventory convention
claims.fact: Multiply source hypercharge by6 and chi charge by5 jointly over the complete spectrum. Standard family chi charges become (-1,-1,3,3,-1); N=-5, H=2, phi=10, hidden flavour charges (-10,0,10,0). Three ordinary SM families are inherited; the source independently fixes exactly three N_i.

claims.locator: PDF pp.1-2 Table I and 2LF/1LF discussion; pp.4-5 Other Models
claims.fact: Retain independent microscopic quarks, not dependent confined hadrons as additional matter. Coloured-X frameworks on pp.4-5 are separate alternatives, not appended to Table I.

limitations: Numerical n_v=3,k=0,q_+=-2 source benchmark only. The generic free-rank family and arbitrary continuous kinetic-generator mixing are not collapsed into this member.
Table N charge is retained in the common LH coordinate, not conjugated twice because the prose calls the physical species right-handed.

papers.limitations:
Only supplied pdftotext text was available; no page images were inspected. Equation layout was reconstructed where unambiguous from surrounding prose. Section 2 lists multiplets and component charges but does not explicitly tabulate all representation triples; hypercharges below are identified as agent inferences using Q = T3 + Y. Allowed mixing terms are recorded in the paper's broken-electroweak, weak-eigenstate mass-matrix convention, rather than inventing an unbroken-phase operator normalization. The apparent (B Y) entry Xbb^R = −sL^2 in Table 3 (PDF p. 25) conflicts with the right-handed-mixing dependence described in Section 8 (PDF pp. 20–21); that entry is not silently corrected or used for an extracted numerical coupling. Appendix B also contains apparent transcription or source anomalies, including mT in the Y width prefactor in Eq. (29); decay-width formulas are outside the extraction scope. No DOI or original submission date is established by the supplied PDF.
Deferred variants: Several vector-like multiplets present simultaneously, including custodial constructions or cancellations that relax electroweak constraints; explicitly outside the paper's minimal analysis (PDF pp. 3, 23–24).; Significant first- or second-generation mixing, including exclusive d or s mixing, discussed as alternatives but not retained in the extracted two-state third-family construction (PDF pp. 3, 5).; Additional scalar representations, non-renormalisable mixing operators, and explicit ultraviolet origins of M^0; not specifications of the seven minimal choices.; The (T B) doublet's d0, u0, and maximal-mixing decay benchmarks are parameter limits within the extracted doublet, not additional multiplet choices (PDF pp. 14–15).; Detailed electroweak fits, the two (B Y) bottom-asymmetry fit benchmarks, Higgs phenomenology, decay widths, and single-production rates are beyond this classification extraction.
Extraction notes: No tools, other papers, page images, or repository files were consulted. Reference [20], listed on PDF p. 31, is the paper's classification citation, but the assigned PDF itself provides the seven choices and mixing restrictions needed here; no essential external definition remains unresolved. Common description-independent assertions apply to all seven specifications unless explicitly qualified. Representation hypercharges inferred from component charges are marked agent_inferred; no canonical model identities or paper–model links are proposed.

papers.limitations:
Only the supplied page-labelled pdftotext text was inspected; no page images or attached Mathematica file were available. Several equations require visual verification: the two-Higgs potential repeats V1222; dagger placement and trace powers in (2.3) are distorted; the definition of alpha on page 5 appears inconsistent with powers in (2.6)–(2.8); (2.9) uses VR without a clear aggregate definition; (2.13) contains yNn in a matrix otherwise using yLn; (2.17) has potentially ambiguous coupling subscripts and powers; (A.22) writes LLH* whereas (2.10) writes LLH; entries involving vL and VR in (A.25) differ in placement from (2.11). These expressions are not silently repaired. Table 3's stated n = 2/n = 3 assignments and coefficient grids do not straightforwardly agree with (3.19), so numerical grid thresholds are not treated as unambiguous model coefficients. Full fixed-flow equations, explicit numerical TAF solutions and stability eigenvalues are absent from the supplied PDF; the paper refers to an attachment and reference [4]. The source does not carry out weak-scale RG evolution and potential minimisation.

Inspected Sections 1–4 and 6 for classification, assumptions, matching and conventions; Section 5 for representative scalar and vector examples; Appendices A–C for interactions, representations and operator definitions; selected entries of Appendix D for S, N, ζ and W matching; and the bibliography for cited basis references. Detailed extracted examples cover a scalar singlet with a dimension-five interaction, a Majorana singlet fermion, a scalar leptoquark, and a vector weak triplet.
papers.limitations:
Text-only inspection; no page images or independent physics validation. Several equations have displaced indices and damaged mathematical glyphs. In particular, Eq. (5.12) does not display the flavor-exchange structure present in Eq. (D.11), and the last denominator of Eq. (5.14) reads M_B^2 despite discussing W. These discrepancies are recorded rather than silently corrected. Long mixed-sector expressions also use w labels where Appendix A.5 uses λ labels; those expressions were not transcribed. The box glyph in Oφ□ is restored typographically from its definition in Table 6. DOI and first-submission date are not established by the supplied PDF.
Deferred variants: The remaining scalar, fermion and vector representations in Tables 1–3; their complete field-by-field coefficient sets are not transcribed.; The vector leptoquark X example and the other B-anomaly mediator candidates B and U2; only ζ and W are extracted in detail from Section 5.; Dimension-five N interactions, vector-like charged-lepton and quark examples, and their dipole coefficients.; Mixed heavy-field contributions, including scalar–fermion, scalar–vector and vector–fermion terms, beyond the framework-level scope statement.; The L1 vector-doublet sector, its modified vector–Higgs couplings and detailed Higgs wave-function effects beyond the normalization caveat.; Full phenomenological fits, historical anomaly significances, collider bounds and cancellation scenarios discussed in Section 5.; Other dimension-five S interactions and the CP-odd S-induced gluonic coefficient.
Extraction notes: Only the supplied pinned-PDF text was used. No shell, web, other paper, repository modification, canonical model identification or paper–model linking was performed. All pdf_page values refer to the supplied 1-based PDF PAGE markers; printed pages are generally one less. The abstract and version date are from PDF page 1. References [27] and [28] were identifiable in the bibliography on PDF page 69; no external content was needed because the selected operator definitions and conventions are supplied in this PDF. All normalized_value fields are null; formulas retain source notation with typography restored where unambiguous. Completeness refers to the seed's representative extraction scope, while each selected field description remains explicitly a partial matching example.

claims.fact: The BSM EFT is explicitly four-dimensional, invariant under GSM, and includes all SM field multiplets, with one Higgs doublet. Expand this explicit three-family SM inheritance, not merely the currents displayed in the example.

Table1 has zeta=(3,3)Y=-1/3, and Section5 explicitly assumes only one zeta multiplet. It is one complex scalar; complete conjugation chooses atlas real-module representative (bar3,3;qY=2). Both quark/lepton currents are interactions, not extra independent matter.

limitations: This is the source-defined EFT, not a claim of a fully specified higher-energy gauge UV completion.
Other dictionary multiplets and replicas are alternatives, not simultaneous matter.
